result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-017.md (6 ACs) and docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-017.md independently, then cross-checked the spec's exact expected values against the real implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/event.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/formatTimeInTimezone.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts). The spec's structure is otherwise strong: every AC (AC1-AC6) plus two justified gap cases (AC-cover, AC-catalog) has a live grammY-dispatch case with exact fixture SQL and exact dispatch calls, no mocked Context anywhere (all via bot.handleUpdate against a real fixture Postgres, avoiding the REQ-013 defect class), TZ is genuinely varied in the process env for AC2 (not just passed as a function parameter), AC3 actually snapshots/diffs events.updated_at before and after two separate live reads, AC4's git-grep pattern is complete and correctly scoped, and the catalog label strings quoted in AC1/AC3/AC6c/AC-catalog ("Yandex Maps:", "Google Maps:", "Seats left:", the followCityInvite sentence) were checked against the live apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts and match verbatim. isFinished's and buildSeatsLine's own exact-boundary cases (isFinished(endsAt,endsAt)===false, seatsLeft===0) are already unit-tested in apps/bot/src/domain/event.test.ts and reasonably left un-duplicated live per the spec's own stated independence principle. However, ONE mechanical, reproducible defect blocks the gate: AC2 and AC5's exact expected rendered-time strings are factually wrong for the real implementation, which fails Step 3b check (c) -- a case whose stated exact expected result does not match the code's actual output is not runnable without judgment (TEST-RUNNER either gets a false FAIL against correct code, or has to guess/reinterpret the string, which is exactly the judgment call the gate forbids).

issues.description: formatDateTimeInTimezone (apps/bot/src/i18n/formatTimeInTimezone.ts:20-30) calls `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(LOCALE_BY_LANG[lang], { timeZone, hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', ... })` with no `hourCycle`/`hour12` option. For lang 'en' (locale 'en-US', the AC2 fixture's chapter default_lang), the locale's default hour cycle is 12-hour with AM/PM, NOT the 24-hour format the spec assumes. Reproduced directly: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {timeZone:'Asia/Tashkent', year:'numeric', month:'short', day:'numeric', hour:'2-digit', minute:'2-digit'}).format(new Date('2026-10-01T13:00:00Z'))` returns `'Oct 1, 2026, 06:00 PM'`, not `'...18:00'`. The AC2 spec's expected value ('the rendered time is 18:00 ... and 20:00 ... NOT 09:00/11:00') is wrong for the real output, which is '06:00 PM' / '08:00 PM' under the fixture's chapter timezone, and '09:00 AM' / '11:00 AM' under the New York-local bug case it's trying to rule out -- the AM/PM suffix means a naive substring check for '18:00' will FAIL against a correct implementation, and a naive substring check for '09:00' to detect the bug will spuriously match the (also AM/PM-suffixed) buggy output's hour digits without the differentiation the spec's prose claims. TEST-DESIGNER must actually run the formatter (or read it as I did) and restate AC2's expected/forbidden strings as the real outputs: expected 'Oct 1, 2026, 06:00 PM' and 'Oct 1, 2026, 08:00 PM' (Tashkent-correct), forbidden 'Oct 1, 2026, 09:00 AM' and 'Oct 1, 2026, 11:00 AM' (the New-York-local bug signature) -- or, if 24-hour rendering was actually intended behavior, that is a design/implementation defect to raise against CODE-DESIGNER/BACKEND-DEV instead, not something the test spec may silently paper over by asserting the wrong string as ground truth.

Same root cause as the AC2 finding, applied to the agenda-item times: the spec expects the Tashkent-local rendering of 18:30Z and 17:45Z to be '23:30' and '22:45' (24-hour). Reproduced directly: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {timeZone:'Asia/Tashkent', ...}).format(new Date('2026-10-01T18:30:00Z'))` returns `'Oct 1, 2026, 11:30 PM'`, and the 17:45Z instant returns `'Oct 1, 2026, 10:45 PM'` -- not '23:30'/'22:45'. TEST-DESIGNER must restate the expected agenda-line time strings as 'Oct 1, 2026, 11:30 PM' (Opening Talk) and 'Oct 1, 2026, 10:45 PM' (Doors Open), so the case is checkable by exact substring match rather than requiring TEST-RUNNER to decide whether a mismatch is a spec error or a real defect.

issues.location: docs/agents/design/REQ-017.md §2.1's own worked example ("Oct 1, 2026, 18:00–20:30") and §4.2's worked list-row example ("Oct 1, 2026, 18:00")
issues.description: Not a defect in the test spec itself, but the design artefact TEST-DESIGNER inherited the wrong assumption from: the design's own example output uses 24-hour time, which does not match what its own stated mechanism (Intl.DateTimeFormat with no hourCycle option, en-US/ru-RU locales) actually produces for English. Recorded per core-directives.md's conflict-reporting rule so it gets corrected at the source rather than re-propagating into a second test-spec rework; TEST-DESIGNER should flag this to CODE-DESIGNER/ORCH rather than silently reconciling it only in the test spec.

result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER: correct AC2's and AC5's exact expected/forbidden time strings to match the real Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) output (12-hour with AM/PM) verified by actually running the formatter, not by re-deriving from the design doc's own (incorrect) 24-hour example. Re-submit docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-017.md for a fresh Step 3b pass. All other sections of the spec (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6, AC-cover, AC-catalog, the shared-setup harness, the independence note) were verified independently against the real implementation and design and found correct -- no other rework needed.
